messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging eng-oncall: continuous-batching latency spike detected across us-west-2 cluster. Error rate increasing, 99p latency > 2s. Auto-mitigation attempted: fallback routing to smaller model, but traffic rebounded. Thread created for live mitigation.

mike: acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs from the controller and kvcache metrics.

sasha: saw evictions skyrocket on kvcache-3 around 1729499900. TTL-based evictions jumped and we started seeing large prefix cache invalidations.

mike: logs show microbatch_size jumping to 128 under high concurrency; usually at 32. controller backoff didn't trigger. suspect batching jitter + seq length shift.

nina: attaching snippet of the tail logs:

```
[1729499921] controller: accept request qlen=410 inflight=96 microbatch=128 batching_window=25ms
[1729499932] kvcache: evict_count=48123 evict_rate=1200/s mem_usage=92%
[1729499940] runtime: cpu_wait_ms=45 token_latency_ms=1200
```

ryan: customer impact: a handful of Dedicated customers on high-concurrency routes see errors/timeouts. Hosted traffic still ok for low qps but 99p for streaming is bad.

lex: can we fast rollback the controller config change from last night? It increased max_microbatch to 128 and reduced jitter window for batching. Maybe that's the regression.

mike: confirm: config change 1729412000 set max_microbatch=128, jitter_ms=5. Reverting would require a short rollout; risk of transient throttles.

sasha: mitigation plan proposal: 1) lower max_microbatch to 48 2) increase jitter to 12ms 3) enable aggressive prefix sticky eviction threshold to prevent cascade 4) apply temporary request-level ingress throttle for affected routes (10% shed) 5) route high-concurrency customers to smaller model variant.

nina: +1 on plan. can we patch controller without full deploy? we have a runtime feature-flag path we can flip via etcd.

mike: flipping flags now for canary hosts. patch command:

```bash
curl -X POST https://controller-api.internal/flags \
  -d '{"max_microbatch":48, "jitter_ms":12, "kvcache_eviction_threshold_pct":80}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'
```

mike: canaries look good for 60s. microbatch averages dropped to 40-46, kvcache evictions down 10x so far. latency falling.

incident-bot: auto-notify: rolling mitigation applied to 4/6 controller nodes. Re-evaluating traffic shaping.

ryan: on the customer side: contacted CS for customers with increased tail latency. We'll open SLA investigation tickets for any 5xx spikes.

lex: telemetry notes: continuous-batching runtime emits metrics: batch_size_dist, microbatch_peak, kvcache_evictions, cache_miss_hotness. Suggest we add alert for rapid evict_rate > 500/s sustained > 30s.

sasha: creating follow-up issue: ENG-RI-1298 "Eviction storm detection and automatic microbatch cap". Link: https://git.internal/ENG-RI-1298

mike: hotfix verified across canaries and prod roll started. Applying to remaining 2 nodes.

nina: rolling apply done. avg 99p latency dropped from 2.3s to 380ms on affected routes. error rate returned to baseline.

mike: next steps: - run postmortem - backport safe rollback to last config - create automated safety that throttles max_microbatch when kvcache mem > 85% - notify affected customers with timeline.

ryan: customer impact summary for postmortem: "Between 1729499900 and 1729500600 certain high-concurrency routes experienced elevated latency and transient 5xxs due to kvcache eviction storm caused by recent controller batching config. Mitigation reduced impact; no data loss. Dedicated customers A,B showed increased latency; CS has outreach in progress."

lex: handing off to next oncall: @oncall-next — I've left the rollback flag and escalation checklist in the incident doc. Capture anything else?

oncall-next: taking over. will monitor overnight and own postmortem. thanks team.

mike: closing live mitigation thread. tagging followups for infra + runtime. :white_check_mark:
